column3: “Our water for money we have drunk” is rendered “We have to pay for our drinking water.”
“At our neck we have been pursued” is rendered “Our pursuers are at our necks.”
The written text has “and not they … and we”; NASB follows the reading tradition.
“With our life” is rendered “at the risk of our lives.”
“A mill they have lifted” is rendered “worked at the grinding mill.”
“Unless” follows a difficult Hebrew phrase; the meaning is uncertain.
